title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
abstract: arXiv:2611.34816v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Initialization determines the optimization "fate" of a model, going far beyond just setting the scale of its weights. It establishes a fundamental initial geometry over the input data, dictating certain aspects such as which examples are considered close and which representations gradient descent will naturally refine first. In this paper, we view the initial geometry of a network as an optimization prior and ask whether a network can change its optimization prior by referencing a completely different architecture. To investigate this question, we use an initialization procedure where a target network is aligned to the representational geometry of a randomly initialized guide network before any downstream training occurs. Crucially, alignment to the guide network cannot transfer learned features, never receives gradients, and does not use labels. We demonstrate that this cross-architecture transfer of "fate" benefits the target network

translated_title: 将架构作为优化先验进行迁移
translated_abstract: 初始化决定了模型的优化“命运”，其作用远不止是设置权重的尺度。它在输入数据上建立了一种基本的初始几何结构，决定了诸如哪些样本被视为相近、以及梯度下降会自然优先细化哪些表示等方面。在本文中，我们将网络的初始几何视为一种优化先验，并探讨网络能否通过参考一个完全不同的架构来改变自身的优化先验。为研究这一问题，我们采用了一种初始化方法：在任何下游训练开始之前，将目标网络与一个随机初始化的引导网络的表示几何进行对齐。至关重要的是，与引导网络的对齐无法迁移已学习的特征、从不接收梯度、也不使用标签。我们证明，这种“命运”的跨架构迁移能够使目标网络受益。
tldr: 该论文提出将网络的初始几何视为一种优化先验，并证明在训练前让目标网络与一个不传递特征、不接收梯度、不使用标签的随机初始化引导网络的表示几何对齐，可以通过跨架构迁移优化“命运”来使目标网络受益。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that aligning a target network's initial geometry with a randomly initialized guide network of a different architecture—without transferring learned features, receiving gradients, or using labels—acts as an optimization prior that benefits the target network.
